shared_elements: low-relief carving on a dressed vertical stone slab/pillar
animal in profile with elongated body and tail
smooth flat stone field left blank around the figures
in-situ excavated stonework with rubble walling behind
justification: Both are dressed vertical stone slabs bearing shallow, flat-topped relief animals shown in strict profile with a long trailing tail, and in both the figure is reserved against a plain smoothed ground, which is a fairly specific technical correspondence. The decisive difference is density and organisation: A carries a single faint, isolated creature on an otherwise empty face, while B stacks many motifs (arched row, chevron band, birds, quadruped, anthropomorph) into horizontal registers across a T-shaped pillar.
